Les précisions de Marc Paupe, journaliste à France 24.

france24fr.title: Sommet Russie-Afrique : une démonstration de force qui peine à cacher le bilan de Moscou
france24fr.description: Promesses appuyées et signatures officielles n’ont pas manqué mercredi et jeudi lors du troisième sommet entre la Russie et 48 délégations africaines ayant fait le déplacement à Moscou. Une nouvelle démonstration de force orchestrée par le Kremlin qui ne parvient pas à faire oublier ses faiblesses militaires, économiques ainsi que le recrutement de mercenaires.

france24fr.title: Espagne: le rail en question
france24fr.description: La collision meurtrière de deux trains en Espagne ravive les inquiétudes après des accidents similaires entre trains à grande vitesse en début d'année. On va plus loin avec Zyad Limam et Gauthier Rybinski.

france24fr.title: Israël: premières législatives post-7 octobre
france24fr.description: Les électeurs israéliens se prononcent pour la première fois depuis les attentats du 7 octobre 2023. Quel impact sur le maintien de Benyamin Netanyahu à la tête du gouvernement ? On va plus loin avec Patricia Alémonière et Gauthier Rybinski.

france24fr.title: Attentat raciste dans les Yvelines : le procureur de la République anti-terroriste prend la parole
france24fr.description: Le suspect de l'attentat terroriste raciste du 23 octobre dans les Yvelines a été transféré dans la nuit de mercredi 28 à jeudi 29 octobre au tribunal de Paris, en vue de son éventuelle mise en examen. Le procureur de la République anti-terroriste, Olivier Christen, affirme que l'enquête à mener à la découverte de plusieurs armes, le livre Mein Kampf, et des autocollants du Rassemblement National dont l'authenticité n'a pas été prouvé.

france24fr.title: Attentat raciste dans les Yvelines : un élan de solidarité se met en place pour les victimes.
france24fr.description: En France, un hommage national sera rendu, vendredi 30 octobre, à Pengo Bossio Wangi, le jeune homme de 26 ans tué lors de l'attentat raciste dans les Yvelines. Du côté de l'enquête, la garde à vue de Kevin T., principal suspect de l'attentat, se termine aujourd'hui. La petite fille de 12 ans qui avait reçu 8 projectiles est toujours en soins.

france24fr.title: En Israël, le camp de Netanyahu attaque les partis arabes après leur percée historique
france24fr.description: Le camp de Benjamin Netanyahu a multiplié jeudi ses attaques à l'encontre des partis arabes israéliens, en passe d'obtenir un nombre élevé de sièges à la Knesset après les élections législatives de mardi. Il les accuse d'avoir reçu des fonds de l'étranger. Le président Isaac Herzog a appelé de son côté à ne pas stigmatiser tout le vote arabe israélien.

france24fr.title: Espagne : les secours encore en recherche de victimes, le pays en état de choc
france24fr.description: L'Espagne a entamé jeudi 29 octobre trois jours de deuil national après la collision entre deux trains qui a fait la veille au moins 68 morts et plus d'une centaine de blessés.Cet accident, la pire tragédie ferroviaire en Espagne depuis 2013, a relancé les questions sur l'entretien du réseau national et sur la sécurité pour les passagers, après que le Pedro Sanchez a réclamé "l'éclaircissement des causes" à l'origine de l'accident.

france24fr.title: Sommet Russie-Afrique pour renforcer les liens politiques ?
france24fr.description: Le troisième sommet Russie-Afrique a été lancé ce mercredi 28 octobre pour deux jours. Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a réuni à Moscou des représentants de 48 pays du continent. Les discussions sont notamment portées autour du développement des relations économiques.

france24fr.title: Du Brésil à la Floride : retour sur la fuite immédiate du candidat Flávio Bolsonaro
france24fr.description: Flávio Bolsonaro a pris la parole depuis son nouvel exil floridien mercredi 28 octobre. Le candidat malheureux se revendique comme "le nouveau président élu du Brésil", il remercie Donald Trump de l'accueillir aux Etats-Unis et indique qu'il "dirigera l'opposition au pouvoir" depuis son nouveau lieu de résidence. Les explications de Silvia Capanema, historienne du Brésil républicain et maître de conférences en langue et civilisation brésilienne à l’Université de Paris Nord.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Attentat de Trappes : le suspect admet avoir ciblé des personnes "musulmanes, africaines ou nord-africaines"
Sommet Russie-Afrique : Moscou affiche ses ambitions économiques
france24fr.description: Le troisième sommet Russie-Afrique se termine ce jeudi 29 octobre. Une manière pour Moscou d'intensifier ses efforts pour le renforcement de ses liens avec le continent. Vingt-deux chefs d'État africains ont fait le déplacement et 44 pays sont représentés. Le Kremlin cherche à accroître son influence diplomatique, économique et militaire, déjà déployé notamment au Mali, au Burkina Faso et au Niger.

france24fr.title: Midterms : Barack Obama mobilisé pour la campagne démocrate
france24fr.description: L'ancien président américain Barack Obama, mobilisé pour trois meetings de campagne cette semaine du 26 octobre. À l'approche d'un vote incertain pour le Parti républicain, le 44e président des États-Unis a mis tout son poids dans la balance, le mercredi 28 octobre en Géorgie, pour apporter son appui au sénateur démocrate Jon Ossoff.

france24fr.title: Brésil : le sénateur Flávio Bolsonaro affirme être "le véritable président" du pays
france24fr.description: Le sénateur brésilien Flávio Bolsonaro, qui a fui aux États-Unis après sa défaite à l'élection présidentielle, a affirmé mercredi 28 octobre être le "véritable président du Brésil", dans un communiqué "au peuple brésilien et à la communauté internationale" publié sur ses réseaux sociaux.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Christine Lagarde va quitter la présidence de la Banque centrale européenne avant la fin de son mandat
Christine Lagarde va quitter la présidence de la BCE avant la fin de son mandat
france24fr.description: La présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, Christine Lagarde, quittera ses fonctions le 7 février 2027, soit près de neuf mois avant l'expiration de son mandat, a déclaré la BCE jeudi. Cette annonce intervient ‌quelques heures ​avant une décision de politique monétaire de ​l'institution, ​qui ​devrait laisser ses ​taux inchangés.

france24fr.title: Espagne : collision mortelle entre deux trains
france24fr.description: Au moins 64 personnes ont été tuées et plusieurs autres blessées dans la collision mercredi de deux trains à environ 150 km au sud de Madrid, selon les autorités, bilan provisoire qui en fait une des pires catastrophes ferroviaires en Espagne après un précédent drame en janvier.

france24fr.title: Informatique quantique : la pépite française Alice & Bob défie Google
france24fr.description: La start-up française Alice & Bob annonce une avancée majeure dans la course à l'ordinateur quantique. Invité de France 24, son président exécutif Élie Girard explique comment cette technologie pourrait révolutionner la médecine, mais aussi menacer la sécurité de nos données.

zeit.description: Nach der Distanzierung von den »Gen Z regelt«-Protesten plant die Bundesschülerkonferenz eine eigene Demonstration. Auch Niedersachsens Landesschülerrat geht auf Abstand.

zeit.title: Zugunglück in Spanien: Rettungskräfte suchen nach Zugunglück mit Kränen nach Vermissten
zeit.description: In Spanien hat nach dem schweren Zugunglück in der Provinz Toledo eine dreitägige Staatstrauer begonnen. Die Suche nach Toten und Verletzten läuft weiter.

zeit.description: Die Präsidentin der Europäischen Zentralbank wird ihre Amtszeit vorzeitig beenden. Seit Monaten war über ihren Rücktritt spekuliert worden.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Mindestens 13 Tote nach russischem Angriff auf Bahnhof in Dnipro
zeit.description: Die Ukraine meldet Tote und Verletzte nach einem Drohnenangriff auf den Bahnhof Dnipro. Russland und die Ukraine haben Hilfsmissionen nach Oleschky entsandt. Das Liveblog

nzz.title: Der Milliardenverlust von VW erhöht den Spardruck im Konzern
nzz.description: Europas grösster Autobauer leidet unter der Schwächer von Porsche und dem Einbruch des China-Geschäfts. In der Debatte um die Sanierung kann das dem Management Rückenwind verleihen.

nzz.title: Christoph Spycher gibt 2027 operative Verantwortung bei YB ab
nzz.description: Christoph Spycher wird seine operativen Aufgaben bei den Young Boys voraussichtlich im September 2027 abgeben, aber weiterhin Verwaltungsrat des Berner Klubs verbleiben.

nzz.title: Neuerliches Zugunglück in Spanien: Mindestens 69 Tote bei Auffahrunfall zweier Hochgeschwindigkeitszüge
nzz.description: Der Verkehrsminister Óscar Puente spricht von einer «unerklärlichen» und «falschen» Entscheidung der Bahnleitstelle. Das Unglück erinnert auch an eine Katastrophe im Januar. Wurden Sicherheitsmängel weiter ignoriert?

nzz.title: Aus dieser Kirche in Palermo wurde 1969 ein Altarbild von Caravaggio geraubt – steht es im Tresor einer Schweizer Bank?
nzz.description: Eine Geschichte über eine klaffende Wunde, unzureichende Ermittlungen – und über Menschen, die nie aufgegeben haben, nach dem verschwundenen Meisterwerk zu suchen.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Eine Fussgängerin stirbt in der Stadt Zürich nach einer Kollision mit einem Tram
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: Smog über Südostasien: Rauch aus Indonesien verärgert die Nachbarländer
nzz.description: Die Waldbrände in Indonesien sorgen für Smog in den Städten – nicht nur in Indonesien, sondern auch bei den Nachbarn. Sie werden zunehmend zum politischen Problem.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Ungleichheit von oben
nzz.description: Johnny Miller fotografiert Orte, an denen Arm auf Reich trifft. Seine Bilder machen Grenzen sichtbar, die man nur aus der Vogelperspektive sieht.

nzz.title: EZB-Präsidentin Christine Lagarde tritt vorzeitig im Februar zurück
nzz.description: Ihre achtjährige Amtszeit wäre regulär Ende Oktober 2027 ausgelaufen. Mit dem vorzeitigen Rücktritt am 7. Februar verschafft Lagarde der Politik Zeit für die Regelung ihrer Nachfolge. Denn die Sorge vor eurokritischen Rechtspopulisten ist gross.

nzz.title: Märchen auf dem Baseballfeld, Arbeitskampf hinter den Kulissen – nach der World Series droht der Lockout
nzz.description: Im Duell der Aussenseiter gewinnen die Milwaukee Brewers den Titel gegen die Tampa Bay Rays. Der Streit um eine Lohnobergrenze sorgt jedoch für Störgeräusche.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Welche vier Fragen sich jeder stellen sollte, um psychisch stabil zu bleiben
nzz.description: Depression, Angsterkrankung, Demenz: Jede vierte Person bekommt im Laufe ihres Lebens eine mentale Erkrankung. Der Psychiater Peter Falkai kennt Strategien, um dagegen vorzubeugen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Drei Tanker in Strasse von Hormuz auf Minen aufgelaufen
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Crans-Montana: Nach mutmasslicher Gewalt durch Ehemann soll Jessica Moretti nicht mehr vernehmungsfähig sein
nzz.description: In der Bar «Le Constellation» in Crans-Montana im Wallis ist es in der Neujahrsnacht zu einem verheerenden Brand gekommen. 41 Personen sind ums Leben gekommen. Die Ermittlungen laufen. Das sind die neuesten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Krise bei Volkswagen: VW meldet neuen Milliardenverlust
nzz.description: Der Volkswagen-Konzern steht vor einem einschneidenden Umbau. Bis 2030 wird Europas grösster Autobauer 50 000 weitere Stellen abbauen. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der vergoldete Makel: wieso die Verklärung von ADHS und Autismus zur «Superkraft» gefährlich ist
nzz.description: Wer heute wahrgenommen werden will, muss einzigartig sein. Dabei deutet man selbst psychische Störungen positiv um. Eine Gesellschaft, die solche Selbstdarstellungen belohnt, verharmlost wirkliches Leiden.

nzz.title: Netanyahu braucht Partner. Doch kaum jemand will noch mit ihm regieren
nzz.description: Die Wahl in Israel hat keine klare Mehrheit gebracht. Ministerpräsident Benjamin Netanyahu könnte deshalb eine Regierung mit der Opposition bilden. Doch die Oppositionspolitiker haben viele Gründe, dem Ministerpräsidenten zu misstrauen.

spiegel.title: Barack Obama: Ex-Präsident verspottet Donald-Trump-Regierung im Wahlkampf
spiegel.description: Barack Obama nimmt sich Donald Trump vor – schon wieder. Beim Wahlkampf für die Demokraten in Georgia walzt er genüßlich seinen Vergleich des Weißen Hauses mit einer Fastfood-Kette aus.

spiegel.title: Porsche: Macan-Nachfolger kommt wieder mit altem Namen
spiegel.description: Der Produktionsstopp des SUV-Modells Macan mit Verbrennungsmotor hat bei Porsche eine schmerzhafte Lücke gerissen. Der Nachfolger soll, anders als ursprünglich geplant, unter seinem alten Namen auf den Markt kommen.

spiegel.title: Elif Eralp sagt, sie werde sich von niemandem einschücht
spiegel.description: Das neu gewählte Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus ist erstmals zusammengetreten. In einer Sitzungspause hat sich Elif Eralp zur SPIEGEL-Recherche geäußert.

spiegel.title: China: Kommunistische Partei schließt 33 Funktionäre aus
spiegel.description: Die Kommunistische Partei Chinas hat Dutzende Funktionäre aus ihren Reihen entfernt. Darunter ein ehemaliges Politbüro-Mitglied, ein früherer Spitzengeneral und ein Ex-Diplomat.

spiegel.title: Shell und TotalEnergies: Quartalsgewinne dank hohem Rohölpreis verdoppelt
spiegel.description: Sie profitieren von den Konflikten im Nahen und Mittleren Osten: Die Ölkonzerne Shell und TotalEnergies konnten ihre Quartalsgewinne auf Milliardensummen verdoppeln.

spiegel.title: Spanien: Funkverkehr deutet offenbar auf Fehler vor tödlichem Zugunglück hin
spiegel.description: In Spanien wird die Suche nach möglichen weiteren Opfern des schweren Zugunglücks fortgesetzt. Medienberichten zufolge gab es vor der Katastrophe womöglich eine folgenschwere Fehlentscheidung in der Leitstelle.

spiegel.title: Jan Böhmermann: »ZDF Magazin Royale« laut ZDF-Intendant Himmler »vielleicht am Ende zu fanatisch«
spiegel.description: Vor dem Aus für das »ZDF Magazin Royale« mit Jan Böhmermann zieht Intendant Norbert Himmler eine gemischte Bilanz. Ihm sei nicht verborgen geblieben, was die Sendung »im Guten wie im Schlechten ausgelöst hat«.

spiegel.title: Südkorea: Nordkorea testet ballistische Kurzstreckenraketen
spiegel.description: Nordkorea hat laut dem südkoreanischen Militär zehn ballistische Kurzstreckenraketen in Richtung des Japanischen Meers starten lassen. Sie sollen auch Atomsprengköpfe transportieren können.

spiegel.title: Kanadas Mark Carney: Donald Trumps Widersacher ist Europas neuer Bestie
spiegel.description: Kanadas Regierungschef Mark Carney trotzt Donald Trump und schlägt eine neue Weltordnung vor. In Europa wird er als Hoffnungsträger bejubelt – zu Recht?

spiegel.title: Elif Eralp: CDU fordert Ende rot-grün-roter Gespräche
spiegel.description: Die SPIEGEL-Recherche über Elif Eralps Angst vor Terrorsympathisanten in Berlin sorgt für Aufsehen. Die CDU fordert das Ende der rot-grün-roten Regierungsbildung. SPD-Innensenatorin Spranger verspricht Schutz.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg – Oleschky: Waffenruhe hält weiter, Evakuierung wird vorbereitet
spiegel.description: In der südukrainischen Frontstadt Oleschky drohte eine Hungerkatastrophe. Dann einigten sich Russland und die Ukraine auf eine Kampfpause. Am Wochenende startet eine bisher einmalige Hilfsaktion.

spiegel.title: EZB-Chefin Christine Lagarde tritt vorzeitig zurück
spiegel.description: Christine Lagarde legt ihr Amt am 7. Februar 2027 nieder. Ihre achtjährige Amtszeit an der Spitze der Europäischen Zentralbank wäre regulär erst Ende Oktober 2027 ausgelaufen. Spekulationen über den Rückzug der EZB-Chefin gibt es seit Monaten.

spiegel.title: Studie zeigt Zusammenhang zwischen Rang und Risikobereitschaft bei Schimpansen und Menschen
spiegel.description: Wer führt, wagt mehr. Einen Zusammenhang zwischen Rang und Risikobereitschaft gibt es laut einem internationalen Forschungsteam bei Schimpansen wie auch bei Menschen.

spiegel.title: Neustadt am Rübenberge: Mutmaßlicher Fahrer nach Auto-Angriff festgenommen
spiegel.description: Der Mann, der in Niedersachsen in eine Menschengruppe gefahren sein soll, wurde gefasst. Die Polizei korrigierte zugleich ihre Angaben zu drei zuvor gemeldeten Festnahmen.

spiegel.title: ZDF-Reporterin Lili Engels: Über beleidigte Bundestrainer und große Philosophen
spiegel.description: Ihr Nagelsmann-Interview bei der WM hat die ZDF-Reporterin Lili Engels bekannt gemacht. Hier spricht sie über den Fluch und Segen von Nähe und die Kunst, Jürgen Klopp zu befragen.

spiegel.title: »Gen Z regelt«: Bundesschülerkonferenz plant eigenen Protest am 20. November
spiegel.description: Die Initiative »Gen Z regelt« will am Samstag bundesweit Zehntausende junge Menschen zu Demonstrationen bewegen. Die Bundesschülerkonferenz will eigene Wege gehen – auch aus Sorge vor Krawallen.

spiegel.title: Nara Smith auf Buchtour für »Homemade«: Die Tradwife, die keine mehr sein will
spiegel.description: Nara Smith hat aus der perfekten Häuslichkeit ein Millionengeschäft gemacht. Auf Tour für ihr erstes Kochbuch zeigt sie, wie sich traditionelle Rollenbilder zugleich vermarkten und unterlaufen lassen.

spiegel.title: Carsten Linnemann: »Wir müssen rund zehn Prozent einsparen« – Gesundheitsminister schließt Kürzung bei Pflegeleistungen nicht aus
spiegel.description: Millionen Menschen sind in Deutschland auf Pflege angewiesen, doch die Kosten laufen aus dem Ruder. Zuzahlungen für Versicherte werden laut Gesundheitsminister Carsten Linnemann aber nicht erhöht.

observador.title: Kushner acusado de gerir contas secretas de países do Golfo

observador.title: Cometas não trouxeram a vida à Terra, diz estudo
observador.description: Vida na Terra poderá ter surgido de processos internos do planeta ou através do impacto constante de asteroides, e não por cometas que transportavam moléculas contendo carbono e azoto.

observador.title: Samsung multiplica por seis lucro líquido graças à IA
observador.description: Samsung Electronics alcançou um lucro líquido de 75,1 biliões de wons (50.544 milhões de euros) no terceiro trimestre de 2026, graças à boom na procura global de semicondutores para IA.

observador.title: Dois sismos foram sentidos esta quinta-feira em São Miguel
observador.description: Os dois sismos, de 4,3 e 4,0 na escala de Richter, foram sentidos perto das 7h locais. Nos últimos dias a ilha de São Miguel tem registado vários abalos.

observador.title: Faculdade de Medicina de Macau aposta em ensino de português
observador.description: O programa está a ser feito em conjunto entre a Universidade de Macau e a Universidade de Lisboa e pretende facilitar o acesso à profissão em Portugal. O curso está na fase final de acreditação.

observador.title: Pelo menos 13 mortos em ataque russo a estação ferroviária
observador.description: As 13 vitimas mortais encontravam-se na plataforma, apesar do alerta de ataque aéreo russo, quando um drone a jato embateu numa plataforma onde se encontrava um comboio.

observador.title: Moçambique limita importação de produtos cerâmicos
observador.description: Novo regime visa a "promoção e defesa da indústria nacional", bem como o "fortalecimento da autoridade do Estado sobre os processos de importação", procurando assegurar um maior equilíbrio.

observador.title: Protestos contra a mina em Boticas vão no terceiro dia
observador.description: O terceiro dia de protestos reúne pessoas de várias zonas do país. A manifestação já acontece há 8 anos e no dia 9 de outubro os trabalhos foram interrompidos, depois da GNR identificar 27 opositores.

observador.title: Análise revela mercado residencial mais exigente e seletivo
observador.description: A Century 21 sublinha o facto do tempo médio de absorção dos imóveis acompanhados pela imobiliária estar a passar de 107 para 119 dias, criando uma "maior exigência" no mercado.

observador.title: Gordura da barriga pode revelar risco cardíaco
observador.description: Radiómica poderá ser aplicada em larga escala para conhecer a qualidade da gordura, seja qual for a sua localização, ajudando a "personalizar a prevenção e o tratamento de pessoas com obesidade".

observador.title: Igreja deve disponibilizar património para habitação
observador.description: Bispo auxiliar do Porto defende que Igreja deve olhar para o seu património, incluindo casas paroquiais, seminários e conventos, e perceber como pode contribuir para a causa da habitação acessível.

observador.title: Fotos inéditas e manuscrito de Gustav Klimt revelados
observador.description: Doação proveniente de uma coleção privada fornece dados fundamentais para a reconstrução de processos criativos e obras pictóricas que foram parcialmente destruídas durante o século XX.

observador.title: PJ investiga incêndio em restaurante de Viana do Alentejo
observador.description: Alerta para o fogo foi dado pelas 7h13, quando o restaurante se encontrava encerrado. Origem do incêndio é desconhecida e não há vítimas.

observador.title: AIMA. Sindicato lembra reivindicações sem resposta

observador.title: Alunos nos Açores continuam sem acesso a manuais digitais
observador.description: Governo Regional espera ter a situação de acesso aos manuais escolares digitais resolvida "o mais brevemente possível" após várias críticas de encarregados de educação na falta de apoio pelas escolas.

observador.title: Habitação. Como responderam PR, PSD e PS aos protestos?
observador.description: André Coelho Lima critica falta de elegância do PSD no confronto com o PS. Francisco Assis considera injustos os ataques a José Luís Carneiro e critica participação de deputados nas manifestações.

observador.title: Valhalla Spider: 1079 cv para soltar… de cabelos ao vento!
observador.description: Marca de Gaydon revelou o seu descapotável de produção mais rápido de sempre. Engenharia da F1, tecnologia híbrida e ausência de tejadilho fazem do Valhalla Spider um irresistível cocktail de emoções.

observador.title: "Crise da habitação não se resolve do dia para a noite"
observador.description: Ana Vasconcelos atribui a crise aos licenciamentos lentos e a leis desatualizadas. A eurodeputada da IL defende a simplificação dos regulamentos: "Se não conseguimos construir, os preços não baixam".

nyt.title: Nvidia Chief, Jensen Huang, Is Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot
nyt.description: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.

nyt.title: At Least 68 Killed in Spain Train Crash, and Democrats’ Secret Effort to Stack Alaska’s Ballot
nyt.description: Plus, the legacy of Dolores Huerta.

nyt.title: Alaska Governor Orders Criminal Investigation Into Peltola Campaign
nyt.description: President Trump had lashed out at Mary Peltola after The New York Times reported that her campaign and national Democrats helped recruit spoiler candidates to the race. He offered no explanation of what crime may have been committed.

nyt.title: The Red States That Could Decide the Senate
nyt.description: Democrats need to flip four Republican-held Senate seats to regain the majority, but some of their targets are in states President Trump won by double digits in 2024. Our election data reporter Evan Reynolds explains just how difficult that might be.

nyt.title: As Trump Faces Down the Midterms, a Grim Mood Takes Over the White House
nyt.description: The White House has been rocked by turnover and anxiety over the midterms. The president, who is tightening his inner circle, has lashed out at critics, held meandering rallies and feasted on a diet of news clips and “A.I. slop,” as one aide put it.

nyt.title: Cabinet Officials on the Campaign Trail? Ethics Experts Say Some Are Breaking the Law.
nyt.description: As Trump officials stump for Republican candidates facing difficult races, ethics experts say they are being lax about complying with the Hatch Act, a federal anti-corruption law.

nyt.title: How Netanyahu Used Fear, Again, to Win More Votes Than Anyone Else
nyt.description: Despite years of political baggage, the Israeli prime minister outperformed expectations, and his rivals, by playing on Jewish voters’ fears of Arab political power and potential security threats.

nyt.title: With No Clear Winner, How Could Israel Get a Prime Minister?
nyt.description: Deadlock is possible, as neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger appear likely to win a majority. But there are still paths to a new government.

nyt.title: In Israel, Arab Voters Mobilize, Shifting Political landscape
nyt.description: The Arab parties have long been kept on the political sidelines. But stunning turnout by their supporters makes the Arab minority an Israeli political reality that cannot be ignored.

nyt.title: After 28 Years Walking the Globe, Karl Bushby Is Almost Home
nyt.description: Karl Bushby has walked 31,000 miles, crossing some of the world’s harshest landscapes. He plans to reach his mother’s house in England next week.

nyt.title: Christine Lagarde to Step Down as President of European Central Bank
nyt.description: Her plan to depart in February, months before the end of an eight-year term, sets in motion a selection process among European leaders for a new central bank president.

nyt.title: In Moving Gradually, Fed Risks Having to Play Catch-Up to Quell Inflation
nyt.description: Federal Reserve officials are expected to restart rate increases in December, but the cadence of additional moves will depend on the data.

nyt.title: A Ukrainian City in the Kill Zone Relishes a Moment of Peace
nyt.description: A rare localized peace deal announced by the first lady, Melania Trump, offered a brief respite for Kherson, where Russian drones and artillery have long terrorized civilians.

nyt.title: Ilhan Omar Investigation Involves New Scrutiny of Long-Disputed Marriage
nyt.description: Several current and former law enforcement officials said an Obama-era investigation found some evidence that Ms. Omar had entered into a sham marriage with a man who may have been her brother.

nyt.title: The Five-Borough Route: The Beating Heart of the NYC Marathon
nyt.description: When the event’s five co-founders first proposed moving it out of Central Park, it seemed impossible. Much has changed in the sport and the city since that 1976 race.

nyt.title: At NYC Marathon, Cowbells Are a Signature Sound. But Why?
nyt.description: Screaming fans and clanging cowbells have become the soundtrack to the New York City Marathon and to sporting events around the world.

nyt.title: New York City Marathon Weather Forecast: Warmer Temperatures Than Normal
nyt.description: Thousands of runners will take part in the New York City Marathon on Sunday. Temperatures are expected to be unusually warm for November.

nyt.title: Spain Crash Investigators Focus on Train Traffic Controllers’ Role
nyt.description: After the country’s second major rail disaster in a year, Spaniards were confronting questions about the safety of their once-vaunted rail system.

npr.title: GDP report to give insight before Election Day. And, Israel's election is deadlocked
npr.description: Economists expect the GDP report to show economic growth, but say that growth is "fragile." And, after 90% of the votes in Israel have been counted, no clear winner has emerged.

npr.title: How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
npr.description: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.

npr.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
npr.description: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.

npr.title: Brazilian political drama unfolds as defeated Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami
npr.description: Defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in Brazil.

npr.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
npr.description: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

npr.title: Dozens are dead in a high-speed train crash in Spain
npr.description: The toll is rising after a high-speed train between slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped south of Madrid, derailing two cars. It was Spain's second major train accident this year.

npr.title: Trump's relationship with Putin comes under fire ahead of the midterms
npr.description: President Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin is under scrutiny again as the president makes deals with Moscow ahead of the midterms.

npr.title: Partial results from Israel's contentious election show no clear winner
npr.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was leading opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties had a strong showing, and a key question now is whether Eisenkot's bloc will consider forming a coalition with them.

npr.title: Ex-Israeli diplomat calls opposition's refusal to work with Arab parties 'reckless'

phys-org.description: A new study has found that in U.S. counties that ended COVID-19 pandemic-era Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Emergency Allotments, child maltreatment rates went up. The findings from the study in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine suggest that changes to food assistance programs have consequences that extend beyond food security and also affect child and family well-being.

phys-org.description: When we think about Europe's winter weather, the Indian Ocean is probably not the first place we look. We might picture Atlantic storms, cold air arriving from the north or rain sweeping across the Mediterranean. In my research, however, I look at how these familiar weather systems fit into a much larger climate system. My colleagues and I asked whether an ocean thousands of kilometers away could leave a detectable signature on Europe's early winter.

phys-org.description: There are two lighthouses on Lady Elliot Island, at the southernmost tip of Australia's Great Barrier Reef. The first was built in 1873, but was decommissioned in 1995 when the second took over the job of warning ships off the reef. Visitors to the island, however, regularly report seeing signs of a third lighthouse. At night the beams of a nonexistent phantom lighthouse are seen far off, shining on the horizon.

phys-org.description: Researchers at Kyushu University have found that an ultrathin layer of iridium manganese (IrMn) can improve two spin-related signals in a structure made of a magnetic insulator and a platinum film. By examining how spin currents are generated and absorbed, the team gained insights into how the intermediate layer improves spin transfer. The findings could inform the development of ultralow-power devices for computing and energy harvesting.

phys-org.title: Atomic magnetism reveals why iron, but not chromium, can produce ammonia using sunlight
phys-org.description: Two nearly identical materials have completely different chemical behavior. Research teams at the University of Vienna and TU Wien studied catalysts that use the energy of sunlight to produce ammonia. Surprisingly, when the three iron atoms that form tiny triangles in these catalysts are replaced by chromium atoms, the chemical reaction no longer takes place.

phys-org.title: Macromolecular crowding could help build artificial cell systems
phys-org.description: Macromolecular crowding can serve as a design tool for controlling the formation and organization of synthetic DNA droplets, a study from Science Tokyo reveals. Researchers investigated this strategy using DNA nanostars and polymeric crowding agents to mimic the crowded cellular environment. They found that crowding promoted droplet formation and enabled control over droplet size, interactions and organization. The findings could support the development of programmable artificial cell systems.

phys-org.title: Explaining the difference between brittle and ductile behavior in polymer glasses
phys-org.description: Glasses are (mostly) brittle, metals can be ductile (plastic), and liquids flow easily. Polymers are interesting because they exhibit all three types of behavior, depending on their chemical nature, temperature, and deformation rate. If polymers are not able to crystallize, their low-temperature state is glassy, and they are hard and transparent. One example is poly(methylmethacrylate) [PMMA], which has been used as an artificial glass since the early 20th century.

phys-org.title: Chornobyl dog population shows genetic signatures of directional selection
phys-org.description: The latest research on the wild population of dogs in Chornobyl reveals that the genetic differences between these dogs and other similarly isolated dog populations are likely evidence of directional selection, not mutation. The work suggests a potential association between genetic selection and environmental variables and could advance understanding of local adaptation and genomic resilience in contaminated environments. The study appears in Genes.

phys-org.title: Could next-gen artificial intelligence help map out future space outposts?
phys-org.description: Planning a successful trip can be challenging, especially when your destination is in outer space. Even before liftoff, space missions require extraordinary amounts of scientific preparation and data analysis to succeed, which can take years to complete. However, as space agencies race to establish a permanent presence on the moon, using artificial intelligence to combine such information into a single system could make mission planning much more efficient.

After an advisory committee narrowly recommended approval, the agency greenlit the drug, Tavneos, and it started making its way into clinics. After uncovering evidence of what it says is data manipulation in the original trial, the agency wants to rescind the approval. But it’s not so easy.

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life

Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

proj-syn.title: A Future for Europe’s Youth
proj-syn.description: The current generation of young Europeans possesses freedoms, material resources, opportunities to travel, and technological capabilities beyond anything previous generations could have imagined. Their demands, however, are strikingly simple: decent schools, secure jobs, affordable homes, and the possibility of raising a family.

proj-syn.title: A Tale of Two Chinas
proj-syn.description: China’s economy is deeply unbalanced, with a battered real-estate sector, weak consumption, and stark regional disparities coexisting with dynamic tech and export sectors. But provided that political stability is maintained, China could continue to be a global powerhouse even as hundreds of millions of its citizens remain poor.

proj-syn.title: Sino–American Stability?
proj-syn.description: Delegates at the Bund Summit in Shanghai largely agreed that the US-China relationship could be entering a new, less contentious chapter, although many were more interested in what the post-Trump era will mean for Sino-American ties. But perhaps the most heartening sign for the future was the honest exchange of views.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Winter of Discontent
proj-syn.description: Although it is true that European integration has always been forged through crisis, the continent’s postwar story was largely one of incremental responses to relatively manageable challenges. Today, the European Union is facing multiple, interrelated problems that challenge its very raison d’être.

proj-syn.title: How Students Dethroned Serbia’s Strongman
proj-syn.description: Following the ouster of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power earlier this year, the world has once again witnessed the merits of “old-school” campaigning. In toppling their own country's strongman, Serbia's new student-led opposition offers important lessons for those defending democracy elsewhere.

proj-syn.title: What a US-China AI Safety Channel Needs
proj-syn.description: Addressing AI safety risks depends on close collaboration between the two leading AI powers, and the establishment of an incident-reporting channel is just a small step in this direction. But success will require that the US and Chinese governments actually understand what is happening under their own noses.

proj-syn.title: The Authoritarian Logic of Selective Privacy
proj-syn.description: Around the world, governments are increasingly deciding who gets privacy and who is denied it, a double standard that turns a fundamental democratic right into a privilege. US President Donald Trump’s administration is a prime example, shielding ICE agents from scrutiny while expanding surveillance of immigrants and protesters.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Chapter in the Anti-Authoritarian Playbook
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s renewed democratic confidence must now be matched by institutional and structural reforms and a willingness to build coalitions beyond the left. Recent democratic outcomes in Hungary and Serbia offer useful lessons.

proj-syn.title: Another Crash Landing for Brazil’s Economy?
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s floating exchange rate, high foreign-exchange reserves, strong commodity exports, and debt denominated predominantly in its own currency reduce its exposure to a balance-of-payments crisis. Nonetheless, continued fiscal deterioration under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will carry high domestic costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Make-or-Break Moment Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has not only abandoned Ukraine and America’s European allies, but has increasingly sided with Russian President Vladimir Putin. To preserve their sovereignty, Europeans must remain united in the face of outside pressure, which in turn requires managing political threats from within their borders.

proj-syn.title: Middle Powers Can Lead on AI Safety
proj-syn.description: With the United States showing no interest in regulating AI, middle powers have an opportunity to take the lead on governance. By banding together, these countries could condition market access on meeting a common set of safety requirements and explore joint investment in technical capacity.

proj-syn.title: Lula Killed the Donroe Doctrine
proj-syn.description: In attempting to disentangle the United States from the rest of the world and retreat into a seemingly controllable hemispheric stronghold, Donald Trump's Latin America strategy had fared better than the rest of his foreign policy. But following a defeat for the far right in Brazil, his project now looks dead in the water.

proj-syn.title: The Wrong Way to Compare Economic Size
proj-syn.description: At the European Central Bank’s annual research conference, Paul Krugman concluded that, when it comes to “weaponized interdependence,” the EU is more powerful than both the US and China. But his reliance on PPP-adjusted GDP as a way to smooth out the volatility of nominal exchange rates ignores the even greater swings in PPP data.

proj-syn.title: Public Control for a Purposeful Economy
proj-syn.description: As more governments recognize the need for greater public control over economic outcomes, they must be careful to define the concept well. What ultimately matters is not ownership, but the state’s capacity to steer economic activity toward strategic objectives in the service of the common good.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Sustainable Livelihoods From the Ground Up
proj-syn.description: In regions where economic activity has long revolved around fossil-fuel extraction, ensuring a just transition requires developing alternative livelihoods that account for each community’s specific needs. Regional endowment funds could be a useful vehicle for funding these local initiatives.

proj-syn.title: The Specter of an AI-Driven Slowdown
proj-syn.description: The rush to finance AI infrastructure is driving up borrowing costs just as governments grapple with mounting debt and persistent fiscal deficits. If the AI investment boom falters, falling valuations could choke off financing, with little room for fiscal and monetary policy to cushion the economic shock.

proj-syn.title: Is a Chinese Implosion Looming?
proj-syn.description: If current trends continue, the Chinese state will find itself exposed to a political succession crisis, a weakening economy, and a lack of resources to exercise power domestically and project it externally. It would be a perfect storm, with far-reaching global repercussions.
